readme.txt.text:
Planetary Data System (PDS)
Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) 
Diviner Derived Data Bundle 1
                                    
Overview
========

This bundle contains the following collections.

  data_derived_ghrm: Diviner Global High-Resolution Mosaics (GHRM)

  data_derived_rcp: Derived Regional Cumulative Products (RCP)
  
  data_derived_pcp: Derived Polar Cumulative Products (PCP) 

  data_derived_prp: Derived Polar Resource Products (PRP) 

  data_derived_gcp: Derived Global Cumulative Products (GCP)
  
  data_derived_gdr_level2: Derived Gridded Data Products (GDR_L2)
  
  data_derived_gdr_level3: Derived Gridded Data Products (GDR_L3)
  
  browse_ghrm: Browse images for GHRM Products

  browse_gdr_l2: Browse images for Level 2 Gridded Data Products
  
  browse_gdr_l3: Browse images for Level 3 Gridded Data Products

  document: Descriptions of the Diviner derived data products 

  document_catalog: Set of PDS3 catalog files 

  miscellaneous: Set of PDS3 index files 

Diviner data were originally archived in PDS using the PDS3 standard, 
which has now been replaced by the PDS4 standard. The RCP and GHRM products 
are new derived products, and therefore they are archived using the PDS4 
standard as new collections in this bundle (urn-nasa-pds-lro_diviner_derived1).
The seasonal PCP product is also a new derived product. It is archived,
along with the newly migrated diurnal PCP product, as a separate collection
using the PDS4 standard. PDS3 labels are included with the migrated diurnal 
PCP products, however the new seasonal PCP products do not include PDS3 
labels.  

The other Diviner derived products that were in PDS3 archives have been moved
to PDS4 collections in this bundle.

Data Products and PDS Labels
============================

Every Diviner data product is accompanied by a PDS label in a file with 
the same name as the data file, but with the extension ".xml", as PDS 
labels are written in XML (Extended Markup Language). The labels may 
be viewed in a text editor or web browser, preferably one that applies 
special formatting to XML files to make them more readable. The labels 
may also be read by software that can interpret XML. 

Documentation
=============
       
The Diviner Reduced Data Record (RDR) Software Interface Specification (SIS) in
the document collection describes the contents, format, and structure of all
Diviner derived data products. As most of these products were archived under
PDS3, the document references both PDS3 and PDS4 components. Currently, the 
revised document has PDS4 updates for the RCP, PCP, and GHRM products.

Text versions of the PDS3 catalog files have also been included in the document
collection to supplement the information in the SIS.

Special Note Regarding GHRM Software Compatibility
==================================================

The Diviner GHRM IMG products and their associated XML files are compatible 
with ENVI version 6.0 and newer. Older ENVI versions may be unable to load the 
IMG products. The current version of ArcGIS Pro (3.2) is also incompatible 
with PDS4 IMG and XML formats. 

==============
This bundle was created and archived by the Geosciences Node of the 
Planetary Data System. Questions about this bundle may be directed to 
geosci@wunder.wustl.edu.

Last updated 2024-02-02.

    CITATION_DESC                  = "Paige et al.,
      LRO DLRE LEVEL 5 PRP V2.0, NASA Planetary Data
      System, LRO-L-DLRE-5-PRP-V2.0, 2018."
    ABSTRACT_DESC                  = "This data set consists of the
      Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment Polar Resource Products
      also known as PRPs.   The DLRE is a surface pushbroom mapper that 
      measures emitted thermal radiation and reflected solar radiation 
      from the surface of the moon.

      Two Diviner solar channels measure 0.3-3 micrometers reflected solar
      radiation.  Three Diviner channels near 8 micrometers classify
      regolith mineralogy by mapping the location of the Christiansen
      feature.  The remaining four Diviner channels measure surface
      temperature in four spectral bands ranging from 12.5 micrometers
      to beyond 200 micrometers."

  
    DATA_SET_DESC                  = "

-------------------------------------------------------------------------+

PLEASE NOTE: The previous version of this dataset, V1.0, was
erroneous in that it lacked any meaningful data.   Please use
version LRO-L-DLRE-5-PRP-V2.0 in your citations.

Data Product Overview 
=====================

The Diviner NASA Level 4 Polar Resource Products (PRP) are produced from 
thermal model fits to Diviner north and south polar observations from 
the first year of mapping orbit. The derived quantities are: annual 
average surface temperature, annual maximum surface temperature, and 
depth to water ice permafrost.  The results for the north and south 
polar regions are contained in separate ASCII files.  Each line of the 
file corresponds to a triangular mesh element in a north or south polar 
digital elevation model derived from the Kaguya laser altimeter 
experiment results (Araki et al., Science 223, 897, 2009). The mesh 
consists of 2,880,000 triangles and covers a square region centered on the 
pole to 80 degrees latitude. The model approach and model parameters used 
generate the PRP are described in Paige et al. Science 330, 497 (2010) and
in the online supporting material associated with this publication. The 
north polar PRP's  were produced using the same datasets, modeling
approach and model parameters as the south polar PRP. 


Data Processing Level
=====================

The Diviner PRP data products are derived from models and parameters  
Diviner Reduced Data Record (RDR) data products.
PRPs are CODMAC Level 5 (NASA Level 4).


Data Product Generation 
=======================

The Diviner PRP data products and labels are generated by the 
Diviner Science Team at UCLA.

Data Flow 
=========

The Diviner PRPs will be made available via a data release 
on March 15, 2011, six months after the end of the first year
of mapping orbit.   

For more information please see the document DP_SIS.HTM
(HTML format) or DP_SIS.PDF (Adobe Acrobat format) located
in the DOCUMENT directory of this archive.

                                      "

Review
======

This archival data set was examined by a peer review panel prior to 
its acceptance by the Planetary Data System (PDS). The peer review 
was conducted in accordance with PDS procedures.

Prior to creation of the final version of the archival data set, 
key elements of the archive were distributed for preliminary 
review.  These included electronic versions of example PDS labels, 
CATALOG files, and Software Interface Specifications (SISs). 
These materials were distributed to PDS personnel, the experiment 
investigator, and others, as appropriate.



Known Issues
============

None.
